ratings_why.fun: Short clocks feeding long ones, a stone total that only rises and a Ribica clutch to chase make a board you watch ripen; the counter load keeps it from an 8.
ratings_why.distinct: A countdown tribe that pays for silence (Robber-Knight) and repeats whoever spoke last (Netopir) plays unlike any current tribe, though 'tick down, then pay' is a known shape.

verdict_why: v2 fixed the loops and the unreadable cards; what remains is one line of Sitter wording and screen work, not a new design round.

points.text: The Seven-Year Sitter doesn't say what happens to a Vigil already counting when it arrives or leaves: does a Vigil with 1 left become 2 left? Add one line.
The flavour lands in what cards do: blind olms take lamps only where there is no Vigil, the bat repeats the last voice, the knight pays for quiet. Keep that as the bar for any later change.
Vigil, Deep Vigil, Dripstone and the lake are four things to track. Show Deep Vigil with a distinct frame so a player can tell at a glance which clocks tick on other endings.
The Pilgrim, Courier Bat and Netopir all react to 'a Vigil ended'; a small flash on the ending unit would let players follow who gets paid, in order.
The Robber-Knight's quiet turn is the tribe's most thematic choice; one more quiet-turn card at Tier 2 or 3 could make the 'speak rarely, hugely' build start earlier.

standouts.why: Brother Netopir, loyal to whoever asked last, turns the order of endings into a readable puzzle.
Gold for a silent turn is a clean, one-line rival plan that fits the cloister fantasy exactly.
Mother Ribica's clutch of twelve is the seed's rare breeding made into a goal the whole board feeds.

weakest.why: Flood-Mark Reader is a plain Start of Combat buff by stone count; it does nothing a cave olm would do.
"Baby Dragon" has a great name but its text is just Attack per Dripstone, the same read as the Olmling.
'Counts as every tribe' is a lot of hidden rules on one card; a player can't know what it touches without checking every other tribe.

flags.note: Effect on a Vigil already partway through its count isn't written.
Counts as every tribe: Shy, Fly South, Ring and Eat edge cases need written answers.
Pale Olmling grows by Dripstone, which never falls; golden plus Sitter plus Netopir could run away late.
Netopir repeating Ribica gives two goldens a turn; worth the owner's eye.
